body.statement:
The sharp annotation frontier is
\[
r_\epsilon(n,m,d)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+
\left(\frac{d}{(n+m)\log(en)}\right)^2\right\}.
\]
There exist \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, uniformly for \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\),
\[
c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\le R_\epsilon(n,m,d)
\le C_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d),
\]
and the upper bound is attained by the total computable \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}\).  At \(m=0\),
\[
r_\epsilon(n,0,d)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+
\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\},
\]
which is the endpoint recorded in \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap/oeq:sharp-minimax}\), not a separate contribution here.  For every fixed \(n,d\),
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}R_\epsilon(n,m,d)=R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d).
\]
Along arbitrary sequences \(n\to\infty\), with \(m=m_n\), \(d=d_n\), the following are necessary and sufficient:
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_n}{(n+m_n)\log(en)}\to0;
\]
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=O(n^{-1})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
d_n=O\!\left(\frac{(n+m_n)\log(en)}{\sqrt n}\right);
\]
and
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=o\{R_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)\}
\]
if and only if both
\[
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt n\log(en)}\to\infty,
\qquad
\frac{n}{n+m_n}\max\!\left\{1,\frac{d_n}{n\log(en)}\right\}\to0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
The two minimax inequalities are exactly \(\texttt{thm:uniform-mixed-upper}\) and \(\texttt{thm:common-marginal-converse}\); both use the same class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and the same fixed two-sample experiment.  Substitution of \(m=0\) gives the displayed supervised expression algebraically.  The fixed-parameter limit is \(\texttt{thm:known-marginal-limit}\), and \(\texttt{thm:known-marginal-boundary}\) identifies its scale as \(n^{-1}\).

It remains only to verify that the sequence conditions are genuinely equivalent to the rate rather than sufficient tuning rules.  Write
\[
\ell_n=\log(en),\qquad x_n=\frac{d_n}{(n+m_n)\ell_n}.
\]
Because \(n^{-1}\to0\), the capped expression \(r_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)\) tends to zero exactly when \(x_n\to0\), proving the first equivalence.  Also
\[
r_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=O(n^{-1})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad nx_n^2=O(1),
\]
which is the second displayed condition after taking square roots.

For strict improvement put
\[
y_n=\frac{d_n}{n\ell_n},\qquad q_n=\frac{n}{n+m_n};
\]
then \(x_n=q_ny_n\),
\[
r_\epsilon(n,m_n,d_n)=\min\{1,n^{-1}+q_n^2y_n^2\},\qquad
r_\epsilon(n,0,d_n)=\min\{1,n^{-1}+y_n^2\}.                 \tag{46}
\]
The first term in the ratio in (46) is negligible if and only if
\[
\frac{n^{-1}}{\min\{1,n^{-1}+y_n^2\}}\to0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad ny_n^2\to\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt n\ell_n}\to\infty.                       \tag{47}
\]
Under (47), the denominator in (46) is asymptotic, up to universal factors, to \(\min(1,y_n^2)\).  The other term is negligible precisely when
\[
\frac{q_n^2y_n^2}{\min(1,y_n^2)}
=\left[q_n\max\{1,y_n\}\right]^2\to0,                     \tag{48}
\]
which is the second asserted condition.  Conversely, a vanishing ratio in (46) forces separately the nonnegative ratios in (47) and (48) to vanish.  Uniform two-sided constants transfer all three equivalences from \(r_\epsilon\) to \(R_\epsilon\), completing the proof.
body.justification: The matched rate quantifies the exact order value of auxiliary annotation information while retaining the irreducible labeled-outcome floor.
body.gap: The theorem joins the supervised logarithmic boundary to the known-marginal benchmark through a finite-\(m\) minimax transition and proves the exact consistency, root-\(n\), and strict-improvement conditions.
body.consumer: Sections 2.1 and 4 of Cheng, Ananthakrishnan, and Cai gain a baseline-only rule for comparing another chart-reviewed outcome with another treatment--covariate record when nuisance models are not trusted.
